tasks.short: Set up participant registration, maintain accurate attendee records and organise check-in.

steps.what: Agree registration categories, capacity, deadlines and exception rules.
Configure forms and ticket categories in the {OTHER} event registration system.
Reconcile registration exports, duplicates and capacity in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve participant questions, incomplete details and registration exceptions through the {EMAIL}.
Send registration confirmations and joining instructions from the {OTHER} event registration system.
Prepare badge files and restricted check-in lists.
Check participants in and handle arrival discrepancies.

tasks.design: Configure reusable forms, capacity rules, confirmations and badge templates in the {OTHER} event registration system. A deterministic integration maintains attendee records and restricted check-in views, while self-service corrections reduce questions in the {EMAIL}; staff handle exceptions and arrivals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event-specific forms, disconnected contact records and late changes made repeatable configuration difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing registration features cover most steps. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining mappings and validation rules.
tasks.still_hard: Late substitutions, accessibility requests, disputed eligibility and unreliable venue connectivity still need practical handling.
tasks.human_edge: Welcome participants, recognise sensitive needs and resolve exceptions without making people feel excluded.

ambition.what: A participant self-service change and waitlist service

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time repairing lists and more time preparing the arrival experience. They can be delegated authority to release waitlist places within approved capacity rules.

reach.task: Measure registration conversion by invitation segment.
reach.learn: Campaign identifiers, funnel measures and permitted contact-data reuse.

evidence.claim: Registration forms, capacity controls, confirmations and badge generation commonly use configurable software.
Deterministic matching can replace routine export reconciliation; ambiguous identities still need review.

assumptions: The company runs recurring events and uses a standalone event registration system alongside shared documents and email.
Routine confirmations use approved templates; eligibility overrides remain with authorised staff.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. No model is needed for the proposed registration workflow.
Access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
Build estimates are working-day effort ranges for one reusable event setup.
unknowns: Existing registration capabilities, export formats and interface access.
Whether events require payment, refunds or identity verification.
Lawful bases, retention periods and handling of health-related accessibility or dietary information.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove the reconciliation workbook entirely?
Which registration exceptions recur often enough to support participant self-service?
new_work: Review exception queues and failed deliveries.
Maintain categories, capacity rules and approved message templates.
Maintain access restrictions, retention jobs and an offline check-in fallback.

tasks.short: Develop relevant event topics, select speakers and confirm the programme.

steps.what: Collect audience feedback, event objectives and previous programme material.
Draft topic options and session outlines.

loop.input: Approved programme source pack with source identifiers and event objectives.
loop.output: Topic options with audience needs, session outlines and source references.
loop.check: Require valid source references and separate supported facts from proposed ideas; the planner checks relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence or unresolved claims return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the options but cannot synthesise varied audience comments into useful themes.

steps.what: Discuss topic relevance, programme balance and audience priorities.
Research speaker credentials and prepare a shortlist.

loop.input: Planner-selected speaker profiles, previous feedback and programme requirements.
loop.output: A comparison of evidenced expertise, topic fit, known fees and missing information.
loop.check: Every factual entry links to a supplied source; unknown fees and availability remain unknown.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unverifiable claims go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Speaker biographies and feedback are free text with inconsistent descriptions of expertise.

steps.what: Approve speaker choices and outreach spending limits.
Agree speaker participation, fees, availability and session expectations.
Update the programme document with confirmed speakers and sessions.

tasks.design: A deterministic collector assembles an approved source pack from the {DOCS} and {CRM}. Bounded drafting and extraction loops prepare topic options and speaker comparisons, while structured confirmations generate the programme in the {DOCS}; people choose the direction, approve spending and agree participation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience feedback and speaker information were scattered and inconsistent, while topic selection depended on context and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded models can organise supplied text into traceable drafts. Small integrations and document generators are cheaper to implement with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, audience credibility, speaker chemistry and willingness to participate remain difficult to infer from documents.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a programme with a clear point of view and persuade credible speakers to contribute.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time testing programme ideas with audiences and coaching speakers. With a delegated brief, they can commission sessions for the new attendee track within an approved budget.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Turn audience interviews and feedback into programme priorities.
reach.learn: Interview design, sampling bias and distinguishing demand from isolated comments.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting and extraction can reduce programme preparation without replacing speaker selection.
Structured speaker confirmations can populate programme templates deterministically.

assumptions: The company retains previous programmes and some audience feedback.
Speaker research uses selected sources rather than autonomous web investigation.
Speaker comparisons concern event participation, without inferring sensitive personal traits.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine any employee consultation requirements.
Build estimates are working-day effort ranges for one programme workflow.
unknowns: Availability and permitted reuse of feedback and speaker records.
Who approves programme direction, speaker fees and contractual commitments.
Whether the event serves customers, employees or the public.
Required languages and applicable consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Do evidence-linked topic drafts save preparation time while preserving programme originality?
Which speaker criteria can be checked from sources, and which require a conversation?
new_work: Curate the programme source pack and remove stale material.
Verify speaker credentials and factual draft claims.
Maintain comparison fields and programme templates.
Collect audience feedback on the new programme track.

tasks.short: Promote event services through association relationships, brochures and other publications.

steps.what: Collect current service descriptions, capacity, prices and approved event examples.
Prepare an association meeting brief and relevant service examples.

loop.input: Approved service facts, association profile and permitted contact history.
loop.output: An association brief with relevant examples, questions and source references.
loop.check: Validate prices and capacities against source fields; the planner checks relevance and removes unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported tailoring is omitted.
loop.why_not_simpler: Choosing useful discussion points requires reading varied association descriptions and contact notes.

steps.what: Meet association representatives to understand needs and discuss event services.
Draft brochure copy and assemble publication layouts.

loop.input: Approved service facts, audience needs and a fixed publication template.
loop.output: Draft copy in defined sections, rendered into the publication template.
loop.check: Lock prices and capacities to source fields; check claims, required sections, text overflow and accessibility.
loop.stop: One draft and two bounded corrections; unresolved copy or layout issues return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout is deterministic, but audience-specific explanatory copy needs bounded language generation.

steps.what: Review claims, presentation and commercial terms before approving publication.
Publish service material and send approved publications to selected contacts.
Record association needs, follow-up commitments and resulting leads in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: An integration supplies approved service facts from the {DOCS} and contact context from the {CRM}. Bounded drafting loops prepare association briefs and publication copy, deterministic templates render the material, and configured approval and distribution flows connect the {DOCS}, {CMS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relationship knowledge lived with individuals, while publication updates required repeated copying and layout work.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured service facts and reusable templates remove mechanical work. Bounded drafting makes tailored preparation affordable without automating association meetings.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, commercial positioning, publication quality and promises about unusual event requirements still need experienced judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what association representatives need and make credible commitments that fit the relationship.
tasks.altitude: The planner can spend more of the week meeting associations and shaping useful service proposals. They can gain authority to recommend standard service bundles within published commercial limits.

reach.task: Maintain a consistent, accessible event-services publication series.
reach.learn: Editorial structure, plain-language editing and publication accessibility.
Typography, image permissions and print-ready layout checks.

evidence.claim: Approved facts and fixed layouts support deterministic publication generation, with models used for tailored copy.
Association relationship development remains human work even when preparation and distribution change.

assumptions: This task applies where the company promotes event services to external associations or partners.
A marketing manager approves publication claims and commercial terms.
Distribution uses approved versions and contact lists with applicable suppression rules.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules govern direct marketing and any employee consultation.
Build estimates are working-day effort ranges for a reusable publication and outreach workflow.
unknowns: Whether the company sells event services or only promotes its own events.
Current ownership and accuracy of service descriptions and prices.
Image rights, publication languages and print requirements.
Permitted contact uses and applicable national marketing rules.
research_questions: Which publication formats can use existing templates without custom layout code?
What service scope would make a small-association advisory offer commercially viable?
new_work: Maintain approved service facts, examples and image permissions.
Review generated copy and rendered publications.
Record relationship context and honour follow-up commitments.
Maintain templates, distribution rules and publication expiry dates.

tasks.short: Plan event publicity, attract sponsors and track campaign and sponsorship delivery.

steps.what: Agree publicity objectives, audience, budget and success measures.
Define sponsorship packages, prices, available benefits and delivery limits.
Draft event publicity and sponsor proposal material.

loop.input: Approved event facts, programme, package fields, brand guidelines and channel limits.
loop.output: Channel-specific publicity drafts and a sponsor proposal using fixed commercial fields.
loop.check: Validate dates, prices, speaker names and package benefits against sources; check claims and channel limits.
loop.stop: One draft and two correction passes; unresolved claims return to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but adapting the message to audiences and channels requires language generation.

steps.what: Select attendee segments and sponsorship prospects in the {CRM}.
Approve campaign assets, recipients, sponsorship terms and spending limits.
Schedule and launch approved event publicity across selected channels.
Discuss sponsor objectives and negotiate benefits, fees and exclusions.
Approve and sign the sponsorship agreement.
Record signed sponsorship terms and assign benefit delivery tasks.
Combine campaign results, registrations and sponsorship progress in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: A sponsorship records app maintains benefit inventory and generates proposals, with a bounded loop drafting publicity from approved facts in the {DOCS}. Configured approvals release campaigns through the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CMS}, {SOCIAL} and {ADS}, while signed structured terms feed delivery tasks in the {PROJECT}. Deterministic integrations combine results in the {BI}; sponsor negotiations and signing stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Packages, publicity, contact lists and delivery commitments were maintained separately, making updates and reporting labour-intensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing campaign and signature features handle releases and commitments. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connecting inventory, agreement fields and reporting.
tasks.still_hard: Sponsor fit, exclusivity conflicts, credible audience promises and attribution across channels remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Protect audience trust while negotiating sponsorships that deliver value to both sides.

ambition.what: A weekly registration-led channel budget allocation

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling campaign reports and chasing sponsorship paperwork. They can gain authority to move spend between approved channels within a fixed event budget, using weekly registration evidence.

reach.task: Allocate event promotion spending across channels.
reach.learn: Incremental results, attribution limits, acquisition costs and controlled budget changes.

reach.task: Assess sponsor compatibility and publicity risks.
reach.learn: Reputation assessment, editorial independence and escalation judgement.

evidence.claim: Campaign scheduling, approval routing and structured sponsorship records can use deterministic configuration and integrations.
A bounded drafting loop can prepare publicity while commercial commitments remain subject to human approval.

assumptions: The company uses only a subset of the listed publicity channels for any one event.
Campaign release identifies approved versions, recipients, timing and spending limits; material changes require a fresh release.
Sponsorship agreements retain structured commercial fields; custom terms require manual mapping before delivery tasks are generated.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules govern direct marketing and any employee consultation.
Build estimates are working-day effort ranges for one reusable campaign and sponsorship workflow.
Run cost excludes advertising spend.
unknowns: Existing campaign, registration and signature interfaces and permissions.
Sponsor exclusivity rules, signing authority and exception thresholds.
Contact provenance, permitted outreach and national marketing requirements.
Available attribution data and authority to reallocate campaign spending.
Whether sponsorship fulfilment includes attendee-data sharing.
research_questions: Can existing configuration provide sponsorship inventory and prevent conflicting benefit reservations?
Which campaign measures support budget decisions without claiming unsupported attribution?
Can signed agreement fields feed delivery tasks without interpreting free-text contracts?
new_work: Review publicity drafts and approve specific campaign releases.
Maintain sponsorship inventory, prices and exclusivity rules.
Resolve failed integrations and unmapped agreement terms.
Monitor sponsor delivery tasks and campaign data quality.
Review weekly channel results and document budget decisions.

role.altitude: The planner's week shifts from list repair, document assembly and status chasing toward audience research, programme choices and partner conversations. Delegated rights can include waitlist releases, session commissioning and channel spending within explicit limits; major commitments remain with the authorised approver.
reach: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: turn audience evidence into programme priorities.
Editors and Graphic Designers: produce accessible, reusable event publications.
Advertising and Promotions Managers: make evidence-based channel spending decisions.
Public Relations Managers: assess sponsor fit and protect audience trust.
skills_to_grow: Structured event data and reusable templates
Source checking and bounded draft review
role.ambitious_version: Run an audience-led event service that combines participant self-service, programmes for first-time attendees, small-association advice and weekly promotion decisions, with human ownership of relationships and commercial commitments.
